svg.title: Platform basics: bulk record work on shared scales — Noticeable differences in 8 of 12 tests
svg.desc: Platform basics: bulk record work on shared scales: Noticeable differences in 8 of 12 tests. Median per test for SQL Server, MySQL and PostgreSQL; tests measured the same way share one axis from zero, so bar lengths compare across tests; tests of very different size get separate axes. Scale 1 of 2 · Same scale for these 6 tests: 0 to 40 s: Save 10,000 new records – 1 worker, Save 10,000 new records – one job shared by 8 parallel workers, Change 10,000 records – 1 worker, Change 10,000 records – one job shared by 8 parallel workers, Delete 10,000 records – 1 worker and Delete 10,000 records – one job shared by 8 parallel workers. Scale 2 of 2 · Same scale for these 6 tests: 0 to 300 ms (= 0.3 s): Load 10,000 records – 1 worker, Load 10,000 records – one job shared by 8 parallel workers, Stock availability list, all columns – 1 worker, Stock availability list, all columns – one job shared by 8 parallel workers, Stock availability list, only the needed columns – 1 worker and Stock availability list, only the needed columns – one job shared by 8 parallel workers. Coloured bars mark differences a user would notice, grey bars ties and differences too small to notice. Load 10,000 records – 1 worker: SQL Server and MySQL noticeably slower than PostgreSQL. Load 10,000 records – one job shared by 8 parallel workers: Tie: no real winner. Save 10,000 new records – 1 worker: MySQL and PostgreSQL noticeably slower than SQL Server. Save 10,000 new records – one job shared by 8 parallel workers: PostgreSQL noticeably slower than MySQL. Change 10,000 records – 1 worker: MySQL and PostgreSQL noticeably slower than SQL Server. Change 10,000 records – one job shared by 8 parallel workers: Tie: no real winner. Delete 10,000 records – 1 worker: MySQL and PostgreSQL noticeably slower than SQL Server. Delete 10,000 records – one job shared by 8 parallel workers: MySQL noticeably slower than SQL Server. Stock availability list, all columns – 1 worker: Tie: no real winner. Stock availability list, all columns – one job shared by 8 parallel workers: Tie: no real winner. Stock availability list, only the needed columns – 1 worker: MySQL and PostgreSQL noticeably slower than SQL Server. Stock availability list, only the needed columns – one job shared by 8 parallel workers: MySQL noticeably slower than both.

g.text: Acumatica 2026 R2 · median of 6 runs per test and database · tests measured the same way share one axis from zero, so bar lengths

no difference you would notice against the others. “tie” means inside the test’s noise margin; “not noticeable” means real
